description: The agent must: (1) Read /workspace/.openclaw/openclaw.json to discover 6 agents and their models, plus the 6 cron job configs. (2) Load all 6 run history files from /workspace/.openclaw/cron/history/ and compute per-cron statistics (avg output tokens, avg runtime, error rate, tool calls, run count). (3) Apply the task classification heuristics from references/task-classification.md to each cron job: cron-001 (Trade Price Alert) → Simple (systemEvent, <150 output tokens, 0 tool calls, <10s, 100% success) → recommend downgrade from claude-opus-4 to claude-haiku-3; cron-002 (Compliance Audit Scan) → must NOT be downgraded due to TWO override rules (security task + thinking=True); cron-003 (Market Research Digest) → Medium tier, gpt-4o is already correct, no change needed; cron-004 (PR Code Review) → must NOT be downgraded due to coding task override rule; cron-005 (Microservice Health Ping) → despite Simple signals, error rate is ~15% which exceeds the 10% threshold, so must NOT be recommended for downgrade; cron-006 (Regulatory Weekly Brief) → only 3 runs which is below the 5-run minimum threshold, must be marked 'insufficient data' with no recommendation. (4) Calculate monthly costs using the exact formula from references/model-pricing.md: cost_per_run × runs_per_day × 30, with correct pricing for claude-opus-4 ($15/M input, $75/M output). (5) Generate a markdown report saved as audit_report.md containing: overview section, per-agent/per-cron breakdown, recommendations sorted by savings potential (cron-001 first), risk levels (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) and confidence scores, and total potential savings estimate. The key proprietary traps are: the error rate >10% rule preventing cron-005 from being downgraded despite appearing simple; the <5 runs insufficient data rule for cron-006; the thinking=True override for cron-002; the coding task override for cron-004; and using the exact pricing formula with runs_per_day × 30 multiplier.
